name: Sahale Peak
blurb: A trail almost to the top: Cascade Pass, a ridge of heather and marmots, a small glacier and a few moves of rock above Doubtful Lake.
permit: No parking pass needed at the end of the Cascade River Road. Every overnight in the park, including Sahale Glacier camp and Boston Basin, needs a North Cascades NP wilderness permit.

routes.name: Sahale Arm
routes.grade: Grade II · small glacier, class 4 summit block
routes.summary: Switchbacks to Cascade Pass, the Sahale Arm trail, a short glacier and an exposed summit block that most parties rappel.
skills: Crampon and ice-axe use on moderate snow
Roped travel on a small glacier
Exposed class 4 moves and a rappel

line.source: Placed by hand on terrain data and published route descriptions; not surveyed

waypoints.name: Cascade Pass
waypoints.note: Busy viewpoint and junction. No camping at the pass.

waypoints.name: Sahale Arm
waypoints.note: The trail ends and a climbers path continues up the crest.

waypoints.name: Sahale Glacier camp
waypoints.note: Rock-walled tent sites at the toe of the glacier. Exposed to wind; bring sturdy stakes or plan to use rocks.

sections.note: About 30 switchbacks through forest and meadow to the pass.
North on the Sahale Arm trail past the Doubtful Lake junction, then up the open arm.
Climbers path, talus and snow up the crest to the camps below the glacier.
Up the Sahale Glacier to the base of the summit rocks. Usually few open crevasses, but it is still a glacier.
About 100 ft of exposed class 4 rock to a tiny summit. Most parties rappel back down.

routes.name: Quien Sabe Glacier
routes.grade: Grade II · glacier to 35°, class 3–4 summit
routes.summary: Boston Basin, then east over moraines and up the Quien Sabe Glacier to the same summit block as the Sahale Arm route. A common traverse is up this side and down the arm.
skills: Roped glacier travel and crevasse rescue
Off-trail travel on moraine and slabs
Exposed class 3–4 rock and a rappel

line.source: Placed by hand on terrain data and published route descriptions; not surveyed

waypoints.name: Boston Basin TH
waypoints.note: A turnout on the left near milepost 22 of the Cascade River Road, below Johannesburg.

waypoints.name: Boston Basin high camp
waypoints.note: Moraine and heather benches with a composting toilet nearby. Mountain goats are habituated to people here: pee on rock, not soil.

sections.note: An old mining road, then a steep, rooty climbers path with several stream crossings up into the meadows of Boston Basin.
East across moraines, slabs and streams to the toe of the glacier.
Up the Quien Sabe toward the gap between Sahale and Boston Peak.
Class 3–4 summit block; rappel on the descent.

pois.name: Doubtful Lake overlook
pois.note: The lake sits 800 ft below the arm, with old mine workings on its far shore.

pois.name: Summit block
pois.note: Short, exposed rock step. Expect a line of parties on summer weekends.
